'''Matisse Vincent Thybulle''' ({{IPAc-en|m|ə|ˈ|t|iː|s|_|ˈ|θ|aɪ|b|ə|l}} {{respell|mə|TEESS|_|THYBE|əl}};<ref>[http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/cpr/19gameday/190324washington_roster.pdf University of Washington Huskies 2018–19 Men's Basketball TV/Radio Roster – Sportswriters.net.] Retrieved January 12, 2022</ref><ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide
 |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 18, 2024}}</ref> born March 4, 1997)<ref>{{cite web|title=DR. ELIZABETH M. THYBULLE|newspaper=The Seattle Times|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/seattletimes/obituary.aspx?n=elizabeth-m-thybulle&pid=174102988|access-date=March 25, 2018}}</ref> is an Australian-American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was selected in the first round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]] before being traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] the following day. Thybulle was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] as a member of the 76ers in 2021 and 2022. He was traded to the Trail Blazers in 2023.

Thybulle played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]]. As a senior in 2019, he was recognized as the top defender in the nation with the [[Naismith Defensive Player of the Year]] and the [[Lefty Driesell Award]]. Thybulle also earned first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]], and repeated as the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Pac-12 Defensive Player of the Year]].

Thybulle is a dual American-Australian citizen and spent seven years of his childhood in [[Sydney]]. He won a bronze medal as a member of the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian national team]] at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] in Tokyo.

==College career==
Thybulle chose to attend the [[University of Washington]] in Seattle based on his relationship with [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Huskies]] coach [[Lorenzo Romar]].<ref name=nemec_09302014>{{cite news|last=Nemec|first=Andrew|title=Matisse Thybulle, 3-star small forward, chooses Washington Huskies over Oregon, others|date=September 30, 2014|newspaper=The Oregonian|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/recruiting/index.ssf/2014/09/matisse_thybulle_3-star_small.html}}</ref> He started all 34 games as a true freshman in [[2015–16 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|2015–16]], averaging 6.2 points, 3.2 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 1.6 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] in 24.1 minutes per game.<ref name=allen_07112016/> As a sophomore in [[2016–17 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|2016–17]], he averaged 10.5 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 2.1 [[steal (basketball)|steals]],<ref>{{cite news|last=Waltos|first=Kyle|title=Matisse Thybulle to return for junior season|date=March 28, 2017|work=CBSSports.com|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/matisse-thybulle-to-return-for-junior-season/}}</ref> but the Huskies won only two games in conference and were {{nowrap|9–22}} in Romar's fifteenth season at Washington, and he was fired.<ref name=clark_02022018>{{cite news|last=Clark|first=Ryan S.|title=After Romar's firing, core of current Husky team opted to stick around|date=February 2, 2018|newspaper=Kitsap Sun|url=https://www.kitsapsun.com/story/sports/college/2018/02/02/after-romars-firing-core-current-husky-team-opted-stick-around/303030002/}}</ref>

Thybulle considered leaving the program after his coach left.<ref name=clark_02022018/>  However, he decided to return for [[2017–18 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|2017–18]] after meeting with new coach [[Mike Hopkins (basketball)|Mike Hopkins]]. The former 22-year [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] assistant under [[Jim Boeheim]] sold him on the Orange's acclaimed [[2–3 zone defense]] that he planned to install at Washington.<ref>{{cite news|last=Waters|first=Mike|title=How Mike Hopkins made Washington true believers: Behind the scenes of his 1st season|date=April 11, 2018|newspaper=The ==Professional career==
===Philadelphia 76ers (2019–2023)===
The [[Philadelphia 76ers]] targeted Thybulle leading up to the [[2019 NBA draft]]. They were coming off a second-round playoff loss to the eventual NBA champions, the [[Toronto Raptors]], and were seeking someone who could immediately contribute to their goal of a championship.<ref name=botemps_12182019>{{cite news|last=Bontemps|first=Tim|title=The evolution of 76ers rookie Matisse Thybulle has begun|date=December 18, 2019|website=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/page/holidayhoops28314000/the-evolution-76ers-rookie-matisse-thybulle-begun|access-date=December 19, 2019}}</ref> The 76ers had Thybulle stop working out for other teams, promising in exchange to select him in the first round with their No. 24 overall pick.<ref name=botemps_12182019/><ref>{{cite news|last=Neubeck|first=Kyle|title=The Sixers delivered on a promise to Matisse Thybulle, and they paid for it|date=June 21, 2019|work=PhillyVoice|url=https://www.phillyvoice.com/nba-draft-2019-sixers-pre-draft-promise-matisse-thybulle-likely-hurt-them-trade-talks/|access-date=June 21, 2019}}</ref> They effectively ended up moving up to No. 20 to select him, receiving his draft rights from the [[Boston Celtics]] in a trade for Philadelphia's 24th and 33rd picks.<ref name=botemps_12182019/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/thybulle-team-gets-pick-checks-many-key-boxes|title=In New Picks, Team Lands Prospects Who Check Key Boxes|date=June 21, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 21, 2019}}</ref> On July 3, 2019, Thybulle signed with the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Team Signs Thybulle |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/team-signs-thybulle |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 4, 2019|date=July 3, 2019}}</ref> On October 23, he made his debut in NBA, coming off from bench in a 107–93 win over the Celtics with three points, a rebound, an assist, two steals and two blocks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401160630|title=76ers top Celtics 107–93 in 1st battle of East favorites (Boxscore)|date=October 23, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 23, 2019}}</ref> After scoring 20 points, hitting five three-pointers, and making three steals in a win over the Raptors on December 8, he joined [[Allen Iverson]] as the only Sixers rookies to record five threes and three steals in a game since 1983.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Carlin |first1=Ky |title=Matisse Thybulle joins Allen Iverson in Sixers rookie record books |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2019/12/09/matisse-thybulle-joins-allen-iverson-in-sixers-rookie-record-books/ |access-date=December 16, 2019 |work=Sixers Wire |date=December 9, 2019}}</ref> On July 11, 2020, Thybulle started uploading a series of vlog style [[YouTube]] videos showcasing the [[2020 NBA Bubble]] at the [[ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex]] in [[Orlando, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Matisse|first=Thybulle|date=July 11, 2020|title=Welcome To The Bubble – Day 1|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_DzaVY5tPZg|access-date=July 17, 2020|website=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Cacciola |first1=Scott |title=Matisse Thybulle Is the Breakout (Mini-Movie) Star of the N.B.A. Bubble |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/07/16/sports/basketball/matisse-thybulle-sixers-videos-vlog.html |access-date=19 July 2021 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=16 July 2020}}</ref>

In his second season in [[2020–21 Philadelphia 76ers season|2020–21]], Thybulle was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]], though he only averaged 20 minutes per game. He was the NBA leader with 3.8 steals per 100 possessions as well as 5.6 deflections per 36 minutes.<ref>{{cite news|first=Marc|last=Narducci|title=Three Sixers all-NBA defensive selections, highlighted by Ben Simmons on first team|date=June 15, 2021|newspaper=The Philadelphia Inquirer|url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-ben-simmons-joel-embiid-matisse-thybulle-all-nba-defensive-selections-20210614.html|access-date=June 15, 2021}}</ref>

On October 29, 2021, the 76ers picked up Thybulle's team option, extending his contract through the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-10-29|title=Sixers Exercise Team Options on Tyrese Maxey and Matisse Thybulle|url=https://phillysportsnetwork.com/2021/10/29/sixers-exercise-team-options-on-tyrese-maxey-and-matisse-thybulle/|access-date=2021-11-03|website=PHILLY SPORTS NETWORK|language=en}}</ref>

=== Portland Trail Blazers (2023–2026) ===
On February 9, 2023, Thybulle was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in a four-team trade involving the [[Charlotte Hornets]] and [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Portland Completes Multi-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/portland-completes-multi-team-trade |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 10, 2023 |date=February 9, 2023 }}</ref> He made his Trail Blazers debut on February 13, recording 14 points, six rebounds, two assists and three blocks in a 127–115 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BLAZERS HIT 23 3-POINTERS, BEAT LEBRON-LESS LAKERS 127-115 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200867 |access-date=February 16, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> In 22 starts for the team, Thybulle averaged 7.4 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 1.9 assists. Following the season, Thybulle would become a restricted free agent, and sign a three-year, $33 million offer sheet with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], which the Trail Blazers subsequently matched.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2023 |title=Sources: Trail Blazers match Matisse Thybulle's offer sheet |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37969795/sources-blazers-match-matisse-thybulle-offer-sheet |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

On October 31, 2025, it was announced that Thybulle would miss 4-to-6 weeks after undergoing surgery to repair a torn [[ulnar collateral ligament of thumb|ulnar collateral ligament]] in his left thumb.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 1, 2025 |title=Portland's Thybulle has surgery on left thumb |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46796669/matisse-thybulle-sidelined-surgery-left-thumb |access-date=2025-12-13 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> Thybulle would make 30 appearances for Portland during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 5.8 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 0.9 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Matisse Thybulle 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3907498/matisse-thybulle|access-date=August 23, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2026–present)===
On July 20, 2026, Thybulle signed a one–year, $3.3 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sources: Matisse Thybulle agrees to 1-year deal with Lakers|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49411523/sources-matisse-thybulle-agrees-1-year-deal-lakers|access-date=August 23, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Thybulle is a dual citizen of Australia as well as the United States and is therefore eligible to represent either national team.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pompey |first1=Keith |title=Sixers' Matisse Thybulle does the little things on the court, in his life, in his community |url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/matisse-thybulle-sixers-rookie-seattle-washington-20191214.html |access-date=February 10, 2020 |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=December 14, 2019}}</ref> When asked if he would represent the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian Boomers]] at the [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Tokyo Olympics]], Thybulle said he was proud of his Australian roots but would not presume he would earn automatic selection.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ben Simmons' 76ers teammate Matisse Thybulle grew up in Sydney... and could be a Boomer in Tokyo|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nba/ben-simmons-76ers-teammate-matisse-thybulle-grew-up-in-sydney-and-could-be-a-boomer-in-tokyo/news-story/e4b575b4e42f9e9717d9586cb7bcbc52 |access-date=February 10, 2020 |work=Fox Sports Australia |date=February 10, 2020}}</ref>

On February 3, 2021, Thybulle was named as part of the [[Australian Boomers]] squad for the delayed [[2020 Tokyo Olympics]], which began immediately after the [[2021 NBA Finals]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Australian Men's Basketball Olympic Squad Revealed|url=https://australia.basketball/blog/2021/02/03/australian-mens-basketball-olympic-squad-revealed/|access-date=February 3, 2021|website=australia.basketball|language=en-AU|archive-date=February 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210202235815/https://australia.basketball/blog/2021/02/03/australian-mens-basketball-olympic-squad-revealed/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
Thybulle helped Australia to obtain their first ever Olympic medal in men's basketball, beating Slovenia in the bronze medal game.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-08-07/tokyo-olympics-patty-mills-leads-boomers-to-bronze-medal/100359056|title=After finishing fourth four times, the Boomers finally get on the Olympic podium|newspaper=ABC News|date=August 7, 2021}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Thybulle is [[Catholic Church|Catholic]], having been [[Confirmation|confirmed]] as a child.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Huard|first1=Brock|last2=Thybulle|first2=Matisse|date=2019-05-09|title=Matisse Thybulle: Finding Meaning Through Grief|url=https://omny.fm/shows/brock-huards-above-beyond-the-intersection-of-fait/matisse-thybulle-finding-meaning-through-grief|access-date=2021-07-13|website=Brock Huard's Above & Beyond: The Intersection of Faith and Sports – Omny.fm}}</ref>

On April 10, 2022, it went public that Thybulle was not fully vaccinated for COVID-19.  This made him ineligible to play in Canada during the 76ers opening round of the NBA playoffs against the Toronto Raptors. "Yeah, I'm not fully vaccinated," he told [[The Athletic]]'s Rich Hofmann. "This was a decision I made a long time ago. I thought a lot about what I would say here. Essentially I made this choice and I thought I can keep it to myself, I can keep it private, but people are always going to wonder why."<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=76ers' Matisse Thybulle reveals he's not fully vaccinated, can't play in Canada vs. Raptors |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/philadelphia-76ers-doc-rivers-confirms-matisse-thybulle-ineligible-playoffs-toronto-raptors-canada-coronavirus-vaccine-030223249.html |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=sports.yahoo.com |date=April 11, 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref>  Thybulle, who said that he was brought up in a "holistic household" with "Chinese medicine and naturopathic doctors" did say that he had received the first dose of the Pfizer vaccine but did not continue on for the following shot.<ref name=":0" />
